hints: The tangents have gradient $2$, so the perpendicular diameter has gradient $m_\perp = -\dfrac{1}{2}$.
The diameter passes through the circle centre $(3, -2)$.
walkthrough:
Radii to parallel tangents lie on the same perpendicular diameter.
The diameter through the points of contact is perpendicular to the tangents of gradient $2$:
$$m_{\text{diam}} = -\dfrac{1}{2}$$

The diameter passes through the centre $(3, -2)$:
$$y - (-2) = -\dfrac{1}{2}(x - 3)$$
$$2y + 4 = -x + 3 \implies x + 2y + 1 = 0$$

hints: So $y + 2 = \pm 2 \implies y = 0$ or $y = -4$. Points of contact are $(-1, 0)$ and $(7, -4)$ (or $(1, -1)$ and $(5, -3)$ depending on substitution).
walkthrough:
Radii to parallel tangents lie on the same perpendicular diameter.
Find the contact points by intersecting the diameter $x = -2y - 1$ with the circle:
$$(-2y - 1 - 3)^2 + (y + 2)^2 = 20$$
$$(-2(y + 2))^2 + (y + 2)^2 = 20$$
$$4(y + 2)^2 + (y + 2)^2 = 20 \implies 5(y + 2)^2 = 20 \implies (y + 2)^2 = 4$$
$$y + 2 = 2 \implies y = 0, \quad x = -1 \implies (-1, 0)$$
$$y + 2 = -2 \implies y = -4, \quad x = 7 \implies (7, -4)$$

Write the equations of the tangents with gradient $2$ at both contact points:
$$L_1: \quad y - 0 = 2(x - (-1)) \implies y = 2x + 2$$
$$L_2: \quad y - (-4) = 2(x - 7) \implies y + 4 = 2x - 14 \implies y = 2x - 18$$
